name: MonarchAreaChart
title: AreaChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts: Chart with AreaMark(x:yStart:yEnd:series:) per run of each series between edges Monarch computes (overlap, stacked, 100% stacked), LineMark on each upper edge, PointMark for lone and inspected points, RuleMark for reference lines and the crosshair, chartXSelection(value:) for touch inspection, inside MonarchChartFrame (accessibilityChartDescriptor and View as table)
summary: An area chart for volumes over time: several series overlapping, stacked so the top edge is the total, or stacked to 100% to show shares, with touch inspection, legend toggles and a data table.
whenToUse: To show a total over time made of parts (traffic by platform, revenue by plan) with stacked, how the mix changes when the total does not matter with expand, or one or two volumes where the filled area helps read magnitude with overlap.
whenNotToUse: To compare trends of independent measures, use MonarchLineChart: overlapping fills hide each other beyond two series. For values that go negative, use a bar chart. For parts of one whole at a single moment, use MonarchDonutChart or MonarchStackedProportionBar.
api: MonarchAreaChart.init(_ title: String, dates: [Date], series: [MonarchLineChartSeries], description: String? = nil, xTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, stacking: MonarchAreaChartStacking = .overlap, referenceLines: [MonarchLineChartReferenceLine] = [], curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = .linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, includesZero: Bool = true, valueDomain: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, isLegendInteractive: Bool = true, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, activeIndex: Binding<Int?>? = nil, dateFormat: Date.FormatStyle = .dateTime.month(.abbreviated).day(), emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), totalLabel: String? = nil, shareLabel: (@Sendable (_ value: String, _ share: String) -> String)? = nil, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

MonarchAreaChart.init(_ title: String, categories: [String], series: [MonarchLineChartSeries], description: String? = nil, xTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, stacking: MonarchAreaChartStacking = .overlap, referenceLines: [MonarchLineChartReferenceLine] = [], curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = .linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, includesZero: Bool = true, valueDomain: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, isLegendInteractive: Bool = true, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, activeIndex: Binding<Int?>? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), totalLabel: String? = nil, shareLabel: (@Sendable (_ value: String, _ share: String) -> String)? = nil, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAreaChartStacking { case overlap, stacked, expand }

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, a heading in the frame and the name VoiceOver reads.

options.name: dates
options.description: The x values, in order. Points are spaced by time.

options.name: categories
options.description: The x values, in order, already localised. Points are spaced evenly.

options.name: series
options.description: The measures, bottom of the stack first: key, label, one value per x value (nil is a gap), optional colour slot and isDashed. The same type as MonarchLineChart.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: xTitle
options.description: The heading of the x column of the data table. Built in: "Date" or "Category".

options.name: valueTitle
options.description: What the values measure, for the data table and VoiceOver's value axis.

options.name: stacking
options.description: overlap: each area from the baseline; stacked: piled so the top edge is the total; expand: piled as shares of 100%.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed horizontal lines with a label and value. Not drawn in expand, whose axis is shares.

options.name: curve
options.description: linear, or monotone: smooth edges that never overshoot.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error, drawn by the frame. A ready chart with no x values is empty.

options.name: includesZero
options.description: Whether the value axis keeps zero when the areas overlap. Stacks always start at zero.

options.name: valueDomain
options.description: Fixes the value axis. Ignored in expand, which is always 0 to 100%.

options.name: isLegendInteractive
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend shows for two or more series.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected index, to share a crosshair between charts. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: dateFormat
options.description: How dates are written in the popover and the data table (dates initialiser only).

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The empty-state message.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The height of the plot; 240 points by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the frame's built-in strings.

options.name: totalLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Total" of a stack, in the popover and the table.

options.name: shareLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "value (share)" text of the expand popover.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value in the popover, the table and for VoiceOver. Default: a number in the locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

states.name: overlap
states.description: Each visible series is a translucent area from the baseline (zero, or the lowest value without includesZero) with a solid top line.

states.name: stacked
states.description: Series are piled in order, first at the bottom; the top edge of the last is the total. Bands are more opaque because they touch. A negative value counts as zero in the stack.

states.name: expand
states.description: Series are piled as shares of each x value's total; the value axis reads 0% to 100% and reference lines are not drawn.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: While the plot is touched, or activeIndex is set: a crosshair, a point on each upper edge and a popover listing the series top of the stack first, with each share in expand and the total under a stack of two or more.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The series leaves the plot and the stack; its legend entry is struck through; it stays in the data table and the table's total.

states.name: gap
states.description: A missing value breaks that series' band; in a stack the series above keep their place. A lone value between gaps is a dot.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: Drawn by MonarchChartFrame at the chart's height.

appearance: Series use the theme's data colours 1 to 5 in order (later series are neutral). Overlapping fills are the series colour at low strength, stacked bands a little stronger, dashed series fainter; each top edge is a solid line in the series colour. Reference lines are the muted text colour, dashed; the crosshair is the strong border colour; the popover is the raised surface with a medium shadow. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: Built on Swift Charts, which draws the axes and grid; the stack itself is computed by Monarch (not MarkStackingMethod) so gaps break a band and negatives count as zero exactly as on the web. Series, reference lines and the curve reuse the MonarchLineChart types rather than new ones. Touch inspection uses chartXSelection and clears when the finger lifts; there is no keyboard inspection, live region or generated summary: VoiceOver gets the data through the frame's chart descriptor. The legend keeps one series visible, where the web lets every series be hidden. onPointSelect, xScale, valueFormat and formatTick are not offered (the initialiser chooses dates or categories, formatValue writes values, the expand axis is whole percentages). Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (shareLabel, formatValue, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is shareLabel.
accessibility: The frame's title is a heading; the plot is one element named by the title, with the data as an accessibility chart descriptor (Audio Graphs and the data table in the rotor).
"View as table" shows the data table, where each row is read as the x value followed by every series and, in a stack of two or more series, the total. Values are the real values, not shares.
The inspection popover is hidden from VoiceOver.
Series differ by name in the legend and the popover and, where isDashed is set, by a dashed edge and marker, never by colour alone.
Legend toggles are switches with a 44-point target.
edgeCases: Missing, nil and non-finite values are gaps, never zero; extra values are dropped.
In stacked and expand, a negative value counts as zero in the stack; the popover and the table still show the real value.
An x value whose visible total is zero has every share at 0% in expand.
A ready chart with no x values shows the empty state.
A single series has no legend and no total.
Hiding series changes the stack and the expand shares but not the table's total, which is the sum of every series.

examples.title: Stacked by platform
examples.code:
MonarchAreaChart(
    "Sessions by platform",
    dates: [
        Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_772_366_400), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_772_452_800), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_772_539_200), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_772_625_600), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_772_712_000), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_772_798_400), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_772_884_800), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_772_971_200), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_773_057_600), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_773_144_000), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_773_230_400), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_773_316_800), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_773_403_200), Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_773_489_600)
    ],
    series: [
        MonarchLineChartSeries("web", label: "Web", values: [420, 460, 445, 480, 610, 640, 600, 520, 560, 610, 600, 640, 690, 670]),
        MonarchLineChartSeries("ios", label: "iOS", values: [210, 230, 220, 240, 300, 320, 310, 260, 280, 300, 310, 330, 350, 340]),
        MonarchLineChartSeries("android", label: "Android", values: [150, 160, 170, 160, 210, 220, 230, 190, 200, 220, 230, 240, 250, 260]),
    ],
    description: "Last 14 days",
    xTitle: "Day",
    stacking: .stacked,
    curve: .monotone
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en-US"))

examples.title: Shares of 100%
examples.code:
MonarchAreaChart(
    "Share of sessions",
    categories: ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"],
    series: [
        MonarchLineChartSeries("free", label: "Free", values: [600, 580, 540, 500]),
        MonarchLineChartSeries("paid", label: "Paid", values: [200, 260, 330, 410]),
    ],
    stacking: .expand
)

examples.title: One volume with a goal
examples.code:
MonarchAreaChart(
    "Users",
    categories: ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr"],
    series: [MonarchLineChartSeries("users", label: "Users", values: [1_000, 1_085, 1_170, 1_255])],
    referenceLines: [MonarchLineChartReferenceLine(1_200, label: "Goal")],
    curve: .monotone,
    height: 180
)
